cases.statement: One female, Case 1 (PMID 31660500), with acute heart failure at 20 leading to heart transplantation.

people.label: Case 1
people.key_phenotypes: acute heart failure at 20 with hypertrophic dilated LV and poor function; cardiac shock and heart transplantation; vacuolization in the explanted heart; Danon-associated eye disease in the left eye; slight learning disability; no myopathy

quotes.quote: Case 1 was admitted to the hospital with acute heart failure at the age of 20 years.
Echocardiographic evaluation showed a hypertrophic dilated left ventricle with poor function and signs suggestive of non-compaction cardiomyopathy.
Mechanical extracorporeal biventricular support was initiated, and the patient underwent heart transplantation 3 weeks later.

The explanted heart was re-examined in 2016 and again showed signs of biventricular hypertrophy and non-compaction cardiomyopathy (mainly posteriorly in the left ventricle), also vacuolization of the cytoplasma was seen (a finding consistent with Danon’s disease).
The ophthalmologist documented Danon disease-associated eye disease in her left eye.
Because the patient had a slight learning disability, a SNP array was also performed and showed a normal female pattern.

phenotype_specificity.statement: Other causes were tested: Sanger sequencing of six HCM/DCM genes was normal, a 60-gene cardiomyopathy panel found nothing in the other 59 genes, and a SNP array was normal. Family history negative for cardiac disorders. An earlier myocardial biopsy showed no storage disease; the explanted heart later showed vacuolization.

quotes.quote: Sanger sequencing of the genes MYH7, MYBPC3, TNNT2, TNNI3, LMNA, and PLN showed no abnormalities.
Targeted sequencing of 60 cardiomyopathy related genes identified a de novo splice mutation, c.557-1G>C, in the LAMP2 gene. The other 59 genes showed no additional relevant mutations/variants.
Case 1 was referred for genetic testing at 20 years of age. The family history was negative for cardiac disorders.
Coronary angiography was normal, and subsequent myocardial biopsy revealed no signs suggestive of a storage disease or myocarditis.

segregation.statement: Not reported beyond a negative family history for cardiac disorders.

de_novo.statement: The authors call the variant de novo, but the paper does not describe parental testing or confirmation of parentage.

quotes.quote: Targeted sequencing of 60 cardiomyopathy related genes identified a de novo splice mutation, c.557-1G>C, in the LAMP2 gene.

variant_type_and_mechanism.statement: Canonical splice-acceptor change at intron position -1 before c.557 (protein effect not predicted, p.?). No RNA study. The paper states LAMP2 deficiency as the disease mechanism.

quotes.quote: The gene defect underlying Danon disease causes a deficiency of lysosome-associated membrane protein 2 (LAMP2).

authors_classification.statement: The authors call the variant causal; classification software named, no criteria given.

quotes.quote: In all three cases, a final diagnosis of Danon disease was only made after genetic testing that identified a causal variant in the lysosome-associated membrane protein 2 gene.
This software was used in combination with the Alamut software (Interactive Biosoftware, Rouen, France) for variant filtering and classification.

concerns: 'De novo' is asserted without any description of parental testing.
Transcript stated as NM_002294.2; the batch uses NM_002294.3.
PMID 31660500 contradicts itself: the case text says Case 1 had a short PR interval without pre-excitation, while the discussion lists Cases 1 and 3 as showing pre-excitation.
The first myocardial biopsy showed no storage disease; vacuolization was seen only on re-examination of the explanted heart.
notes_for_panel: Female with severe early heart failure and transplantation, with a broad negative work-up of other cardiomyopathy genes; de novo status is stated but unsupported by described testing.
